newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end firmer, IMF still talking.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end firmer, IMF still talking.

text.p: NY precious metals ended barely changed as gold trod water while it waited for the outcome of Wednesday's International Monetary Fund board meeting.

Fund officials are discussing whether to sell some five million ounces of gold reserves to help debt relief, but some member states such as Germany are opposed. It was not clear if the issue would be resolved today.
"I would have expected this market to scare the shorts out because it did not look as if this (IMF sales) was going to get done unequivocally," said Dinsa Mehta of Chase Manhattan.
"But clearly the subject has not been laid to rest," Mehta added.
Gold failed to respond to balance of trade data which showed the deficit in July widening by 42 percent, leading to a weakening of the dollar.
December COMEX gold settled 20 cents firmer at $386.30 an ounce, traded $386.60 to $385.50. Bullion was quoted at $383.05/$383.55.
Silver failed to hang on to earlier gains due to a dip in gold midsession. COMEX December silver went out 2.0 cents higher at $5.098, traded $5.105 to $5.06.
Volume in gold and silver were estimated at 28,000 lots and 9,000 lots respectively.
Shortcovering helped boost platinum prices, but volume, estimated at 2,654 lots, was well below Tuesday's official 10,487 lots when there was heavy spread trading.

"People have started to feel that maybe platinum is oversold," a platinum dealer said. "There were a lot of switches yesterday and people realised there were a lot of shorts out there and maybe they covered," the dealer added.
NYMEX October platinum ended $1.60 firmer at $392.50 an ounce, off the high of $393.40. NYMEX December palladium ended unchanged at $122.50 an ounce.
Resistance in October platinum was pegged at $395.00 which, if breached, should trigger buy stops, the dealer said.
